goal: Build the Memory to Build edge. Today build-spec.js has no memory input, and build-implement.js reads its canary only from args.canary (the injection block at about line 1120). After this change both workflows accept an optional args.memory_ref: a repository-relative path to a stored memory-roll run file whose result.roll (or result) is a MemoryRoll. (B1) In build-spec, one cheap read-only agent reads that file and returns { patterns, canaries } under a schema, and it never judges. Pure script code, selectPatterns and formatPatterns in a sentinel block, picks the patterns and renders them into the Decomposer prompt as prior observations to avoid, not rules. (B2) In build-implement, the same read-only extraction feeds a pure selectCanary({ canaries, task, run_id }) inside the '// ---- BEGIN/END fix-loop decisions ----' block. It picks a library canary whose mutation names a path inside the task's owned_surfaces, using a deterministic hash of run_id + ':' + task.id (no Math.random, no Date). An explicit args.canary always wins. The chosen canary goes through the existing canary injection path unchanged, and each task records canary_source ('library' | 'args' | 'none') plus the canary id in the run output. Both halves degrade silently and safely. A missing, unreadable, empty or malformed roll leaves behavior identical to today. With no memory_ref, no extra agent runs (zero added tokens). Separately (C14), every build-implement prompt that runs tests says to run from the task worktree as the current directory and never to copy or write files into the main checkout.

acceptance.given: build-spec.js source
acceptance.when: the sentinel-extraction idiom pulls the block holding selectPatterns/formatPatterns (either the existing '// ---- BEGIN graph-lint ----'..'// ---- END graph-lint ----' block or a new '// ---- BEGIN memory-patterns ----'/'// ---- END memory-patterns ----' block) and evaluates it standalone
acceptance.then: selectPatterns and formatPatterns are callable as pure functions with no reference to args, agent, fs, Date or Math.random

acceptance.given: a patterns array that mixes kinds 'pattern', 'prompt_refinement' and 'anti_pattern' with various sample_size values and ids
acceptance.when: selectPatterns(patterns) runs with the default options
acceptance.then: it returns at most 5 items. Every 'anti_pattern' item comes before any other kind. Within each kind group, items are ordered by sample_size descending, then by id ascending. The input array is not mutated.

acceptance.given: more than max valid patterns
acceptance.then: exactly 2 items are returned, and they are the first 2 of the full ordering

acceptance.given: a patterns input with entries missing id, entries missing claim, null or non-object entries, or a non-array value (undefined, null, an object)
acceptance.then: it does not throw. Malformed entries are dropped. A non-array input yields [].

acceptance.given: selected patterns [{id:'p1', sample_size:4, claim:'X'}, {id:'p2', sample_size:2, claim:'Y'}]
acceptance.then: it returns exactly 'p1 (n=4): X\np2 (n=2): Y', one line per pattern in the form '<id> (n=<sample_size>): <claim>'. formatPatterns([]) returns ''.

acceptance.given: build-spec invoked without args.memory_ref
acceptance.then: no memory-reading agent call is made (source structure: the only memory-read agent call is guarded by args.memory_ref being truthy), and the Decomposer prompt contains no memory or prior-observation heading, so it is byte-identical to today's prompt text

acceptance.given: build-spec invoked with args.memory_ref
acceptance.then: exactly one memory-read agent call runs, once per run and not once per work item. It uses MODEL.cheap, a read-only agentType bound through AT() (for example 'memory-analyst', or another type whose tools are only Read/Glob/Grep, never 'mechanical'), and a JSON schema returning { patterns: [...], canaries: [...] }. Its prompt tells it to read the file at memory_ref, take result.roll or else result, return patterns and canaries verbatim, never judge or filter, and write or change nothing.

acceptance.given: the memory-read agent returns null or throws, or returns an object with empty, missing or malformed patterns
acceptance.then: the run does not fail. selectPatterns yields []. The Decomposer prompt is identical to the no-memory_ref prompt, with no empty heading. The spec/graph/lint output shape is unchanged.

acceptance.given: a memory roll with at least one valid pattern
acceptance.then: the prompt includes the formatPatterns(selectPatterns(patterns)) text under a heading stating these are prior observations from past runs to avoid, not rules. The text comes from structured items selected in script code, never a raw JSON blob of the roll. The Spec Writer and Risk Router prompts are unchanged.

acceptance.given: build-implement.js source
acceptance.when: the '// ---- BEGIN fix-loop decisions ----'..'// ---- END fix-loop decisions ----' block is extracted by the sentinel idiom and evaluated standalone
acceptance.then: selectCanary is callable as a pure function. It uses withinOwned from the same block and references no Math.random, Date, args or agent.

acceptance.given: canaries in which none of the mutations contains a path-like token inside task.owned_surfaces (including canaries: [], undefined, null, or non-array)
acceptance.then: it returns null without throwing

acceptance.given: a task whose owned_surfaces include '.claude/workflows/build-implement.js', and canaries where exactly two mutations name paths inside the owned surfaces and one names only a path outside them
acceptance.when: selectCanary runs with a fixed run_id and task.id
acceptance.then: it returns one of the two eligible canaries. The index is a deterministic hash of (run_id + ':' + task.id) modulo 2. Repeated calls with the same inputs return the same canary, and at least one pair of differing run_id values selects different eligible canaries.

acceptance.given: canary entries missing id or mutation, or with a non-string mutation
acceptance.then: those entries are ignored as ineligible and nothing throws

acceptance.given: build-implement invoked with both args.canary and args.memory_ref
acceptance.when: a task matches args.canary (task_id or spec_id)
acceptance.then: args.canary's mutation is injected, the library is not consulted for that task, and the task records canary_source 'args'

acceptance.given: build-implement invoked with args.memory_ref and no args.canary, and selectCanary returns a canary for a task
acceptance.when: the task reaches the canary step
acceptance.then: the library canary's mutation goes through the same existing canary mutation agent call (same label pattern canary:<task.id>, same prompt wording and ChangeSet schema, with only the mutation text taken from the library). The task records canary_source 'library' and the canary id.

acceptance.given: build-implement invoked with no args.memory_ref
acceptance.then: no memory-read agent call is made, canary behavior is identical to today (args.canary only), and tasks with no canary record canary_source 'none'

acceptance.given: build-implement invoked with args.memory_ref whose read returns null, throws, or yields an empty, missing or malformed canaries list
acceptance.then: the run does not fail, no library canary is injected, tasks record canary_source 'none' (or 'args' where args.canary matched), and every other output field is unchanged

acceptance.given: the returned EvidenceBundle
acceptance.then: it carries a per-task canary record, for example canaries: [{ task_id, canary_source: 'library'|'args'|'none', canary_id? }]. canary_id is present for 'library' and omitted or null otherwise. The field is additive and every existing field keeps its shape.

acceptance.given: build-implement.js source
acceptance.when: the Test Runner prompt (the run:<task.id>:<tag> agent) and each fix-loop repair agent prompt that runs tests (the testfix, fix and impl repair agents) are inspected
acceptance.then: each states that it runs from the task worktree as the current directory and must never copy or write files into the main checkout

acceptance.given: the memory-read agent call in build-implement
acceptance.then: it runs at most once per run, before the per-task pipeline and not once per task, and only when args.memory_ref is truthy. It uses MODEL.cheap and a read-only agentType through AT().

acceptance.given: the header args comments of build-spec.js and build-implement.js
acceptance.then: each documents memory_ref? as optional, including its meaning and its silent-degradation behavior

acceptance.given: the repository test suite
acceptance.when: npm test runs after the change
acceptance.then: all existing tests, including the graph-lint and fix-loop sentinel tests, still pass

out_of_scope: Writing or editing tests under substrate/test/ (the Test Author owns these; graph-lint check 5)
Changing /memory-roll, the memory-roll workflow, or any stored roll under ledger/runs/
Changing the MemoryRoll or any other definition in contracts.schema.json
Creating or editing any .claude/agents/*.md definition (use an existing read-only type such as memory-analyst)
Feeding patterns to the Spec Writer, Risk Router, lenses, fixer or any agent other than the Decomposer
Using prompt_refinement patterns to rewrite prompts automatically
Selecting more than one canary per task, or canaries for tasks with no owned surface named in the mutation
Changing the existing canary mutation agent's prompt, schema or label beyond where the mutation text comes from
Changing graph-lint checks, the boundary check, withinOwned semantics or fix-loop logic
Ledger/Method Ledger updates or catch-rate accounting for library canaries
HANDOFF.md, OPERATING_MODEL.md and COMPANY.md documentation updates
risk_reasons: The spec adds optional args.memory_ref input ('both workflows accept an optional args.memory_ref') which existing callers do not provide, preserving backward compatibility
Additive output fields only (AC-18: 'The field is additive and every existing field keeps its shape') rather than schema-breaking changes
Explicit silent degradation guarantee: 'A missing, unreadable, empty or malformed roll leaves behavior identical to today' (AC-8, AC-17)

Byte-identical behavior when args.memory_ref is absent: AC-6 confirms Decomposer prompt is 'byte-identical to today's prompt text' and AC-16 confirms 'canary behavior is identical to today (args.canary only)'
No changes to data storage, authentication, secrets, payments, or infrastructure

Touched surfaces are workflow scripts only (.claude/workflows/build-spec.js and .claude/workflows/build-implement.js); out-of-scope explicitly excludes memory-roll workflow and contracts.schema.json changes
